method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, tag-branch inspection, formula/token comparison and reverse paraphrase with checked native terminology; not independent or human review.
scope: The propositional-language inventory, primitive and defined connectives, inductive formula formation, abbreviation clauses and literal syntactic identity.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Propositional formulas use a denumerable variable set, optionally primitive true and false constants, selected logical connectives and punctuation; the language is L0. Defined symbols are unofficial abbreviations that shorten formulas and proofs. Alternative textbooks use the listed symbols and names for negation, conjunction, implication, equivalence, falsity and truth.
samples.checks: Every tag condition, symbol, punctuation mark and alternative name remains under the same source branch. The explanation preserves both advantages and the reason more primitives lengthen proofs.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The formulas are the least inductively generated set containing the enabled constants and every propositional variable and closed under the enabled unary and binary connectives. Nothing else is a formula. The staged explanation starts with atoms, applies rules at later finite stages, and admits exactly what eventually appears. Outermost parentheses may be omitted for a binary compound.
samples.checks: All atomic and closure clauses, the limiting clause, the infinite-stage explanation, and the narrowly scoped outer-parenthesis convention are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Each enabled defined truth constant or connective abbreviates exactly the displayed formula in terms of available primitives. The conditional disjunction branch uses not-A or B; the frozen source's unmatched closing parenthesis is removed under MRPL-001.
samples.checks: Every tag branch and formula is preserved after projecting the one documented punctuation correction. The fixed-atomic-formula qualification remains inside both truth-constant fallback branches.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Syntactic identity holds exactly when two symbol strings have equal length and the same symbol at every position. Concatenated strings can flank the identity sign; the example implies A begins with an opening parenthesis, contains B from position two, then the disjunction sign, C, and a closing parenthesis.
samples.checks: Literal string identity is kept distinct from logical equivalence, and every positional consequence of the concatenation example is retained.

limitations: No independent linguistic review has been performed.
द्विसशर्त, आण्विक सूत्र, विन्यासात्मक अनन्यता and the जोडणी/स्वशृंखलन choice remain explicitly prioritized for specialist review.
